class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2" class="section ltx_subsubsection">

#### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.1.2 </span>Trajectory 2: <span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">path-tracing</span>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">

The first trajectory shows a single round of evolution flipping one
task. The second shows how the iteration-5 round, which targeted a
cross-task “post-validation state destruction” regression, raised the
score on tasks the evolve agent had not necessarily named, including
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">path-tracing</span>.

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1" class="section ltx_paragraph">

##### The task.

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">

<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">path-tracing</span> asks the agent
to implement a path tracer that renders a scene description into
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px1.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/app/reconstructed.ppm</span>. The
verifier reads that single output file and compares it pixel-for-pixel
against a reference image; nothing else in the working tree is read.

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2" class="section ltx_paragraph">

##### Trajectory before and after the iteration-5 changes.

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">

At iteration 4 the task scored 0/2. The shared failure mode in both
rollouts was a four-step sequence: the agent rendered a correct
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/app/reconstructed.ppm</span>, ran
a self-check that confirmed the image matched a structural acceptance
criterion, then issued a sweeping cleanup command of the form
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">rm -rf /app/image
/app/reconstructed.ppm /app/scratch</span> as a final tidy-up step, and
submitted on the shell exit code of that cleanup. The verifier
subsequently found no <span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">reconstructed.ppm</span> on disk
and rejected the rollout. The seed harness’s prompt advice against
“destroying verified state” was already present, but no execution-time
mechanism enforced it. At iteration 5 <span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">path-tracing</span> flips from 0/2
to 2/2. In both passing rollouts the agent reaches the same
render-and-self-check state as before, then issues the cleanup; the
shell guard intercepts it with a message naming
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/app/reconstructed.ppm</span> as
protected, the agent acknowledges the message and finishes without
rerunning the cleanup, and the verifier finds the correct file on disk.
The same iteration-5 round also recovers
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">polyglot-rust-c</span> and
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.7"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">large-scale-text-editing</span>,
both listed in the change-manifest’s <span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.8"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">predicted_fixes</span>.
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS2.Px2.p1.1.9"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">configure-git-webserver</span>,
also predicted, recovers only partially at iteration 5 because its
failure mode involves a state reset path that the iteration-5 guard
still treats as overrideable; that gap is closed by the iteration-8
changes described in trajectory 4.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS3" class="section ltx_subsubsection">

#### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.1.3 </span>Trajectory 3: <span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mcmc-sampling-stan</span>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">

The first two trajectories each used a prompt-and-tool pair. The third
shows two harness components from different controllability levels, a
tool-level publish-state guard and a step-spanning middleware, working
together to flip a task that had been failing for five iterations.
Figure <a href="#A3.F6" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 6 ‣ Trajectory before and after the iteration-6 changes. ‣ C.1.3 Trajectory 3: mcmc-sampling-stan ‣ C.1 Trajectories: failing versus passing rollouts ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> summarizes the
before-and-after rollouts.

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1" class="section ltx_paragraph">

##### The task.

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">

<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mcmc-sampling-stan</span> asks the
agent to install <span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">rstan 2.32.7</span>, fit a
hierarchical beta-binomial model to 30 observations, and write the
posterior means of <span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">alpha</span> and
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">beta</span> to two text files. The
verifier installs the package itself and reruns the agent’s
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">analysis.R</span> end-to-end, then
asserts <span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">alpha</span> lies in
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.7"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">\[2.84, 2.91\]</span> and
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.8"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">beta</span> lies in
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px1.p1.1.9"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">\[16.1, 16.7\]</span>.

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2" class="section ltx_paragraph">

##### Trajectory before and after the iteration-6 changes.

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">

The task scored 0/2 from iteration 1 through iteration 5. The shared
failure mode, summarized in the left column of
Figure <a href="#A3.F6" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 6 ‣ Trajectory before and after the iteration-6 changes. ‣ C.1.3 Trajectory 3: mcmc-sampling-stan ‣ C.1 Trajectories: failing versus passing rollouts ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, is a proxy-then-skip pattern
in five steps: the agent computes an independent grid-integration
estimate of the posterior, writes those numbers as the deliverable,
fires the real MCMC sampling as a background job, kills it before
completion to “preserve the already-created deliverables”, and submits
on a final sweep that only checks the files exist and parse as numbers.
The verifier then reruns <span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">analysis.R</span> from scratch; the
unconverged sampler produces values around
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">1e19</span>, far outside the
expected range. None of the prior rounds catches this trajectory: the
iteration-2 prompt edit names a contract-first principle but the agent
already believes the grid integration is a faithful contract; the
iteration-5 publish-state guard protects the deliverable files but
treats <span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">analysis.R</span> itself as an
unprotected scratch artifact. After the iteration-6 changes are
installed, both rollouts run <span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">analysis.R</span> at the full
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">iter = 100000</span> to completion,
cross-check against an independent scratch full run in
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/tmp</span>, and publish the
converged values via the new override token; the right column of
Figure <a href="#A3.F6" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 6 ‣ Trajectory before and after the iteration-6 changes. ‣ C.1.3 Trajectory 3: mcmc-sampling-stan ‣ C.1 Trajectories: failing versus passing rollouts ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> traces the passing rollout.
The task passes 6/6 verifier tests in both rollouts and stays 2/2 for
the next four iterations. The converged values land at
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.7"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">alpha</span> approximately
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.8"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">2.872</span>,
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.9"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">beta</span> approximately
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.10"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">16.43</span>, near the centers of
the expected ranges. The same iteration-6 round also benefits
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.11"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">sam-cell-seg</span>,
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.12"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">query-optimize</span>,
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.13"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">caffe-cifar-10</span>,
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.14"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">dna-assembly</span>, and
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS3.Px2.p1.1.15"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">train-fasttext</span>, all of which
match one or more of the seven middleware patterns.

</div>

<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

and after the two harness changes shipped at the start of iteration 6:
the tool-level publish-state guard <span id="A3.F6.15.2"

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS4" class="section ltx_subsubsection">

#### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.1.4 </span>Trajectory 4: <span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">configure-git-webserver</span>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">

The fourth trajectory shows the evolve agent doubling back on its own
prior decisions. By iteration 7 the publish-state guard had been carried
over for three rounds, the middleware for two, and the score had
regressed from 75.8 to 73.0. Rather than roll either back, the
iteration-7 round patched a loophole in the guard and a salience gap in
the middleware; both patches turn out to be load-bearing for
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">configure-git-webserver</span>.

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px1" class="section ltx_paragraph">

##### The task.

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">

<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px1.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">configure-git-webserver</span> asks
the agent to set up a git repository under
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px1.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/git/server</span>, configure a
webserver that serves the working tree under
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px1.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/git/www</span>, deploy a
hello-world page, and produce a configuration in which the externally
observable URL returns the expected content. The verifier issues an HTTP
request from outside the agent’s shell and reads the response body.

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2" class="section ltx_paragraph">

##### Trajectory before and after the iteration-8 changes.

<div id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">

At iteration 7 the task scored 0/2. The failing rollout reached a fully
working deployment, ran a curl-against-localhost self-check that
returned the right body, and then issued two cleanup commands prefixed
with <span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ALLOW_POST_SUCCESS_RESET</span>:
one deletion of <span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/git/www/hello.html</span> and one
reset of <span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/git/server/refs/heads/master</span>
to an empty state, both rationalized as “leaving a clean repo for
grading”. The shell tool’s iteration-5 guard caught these as
overrideable resets and let them through once the override token was
attached. The external verifier then received a 404 and rejected the
rollout. <span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">git-multibranch</span> failed in
iteration 7 for the same structural reason. In parallel,
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">polyglot-c-py</span> and
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pytorch-model-recovery</span>
failed at iteration 7 with a different but related symptom: the
iteration-6 middleware had already emitted the right warnings about
clean-layout violation and inline-helper validation, but the warnings
were appended only to the tool output, and on the very next model turn
the agent ignored them and published. After the iteration-8 changes are
installed, <span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.7"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">configure-git-webserver</span>
flips from 0/2 to 2/2. Both rollouts reach the same successful
deployment as before, attempt the same overrideable cleanup commands,
and have them refused at the shell layer with hard-block messages naming
the protected web root and protected ref; the agent acknowledges the
messages, drops the cleanup, and submits the live state.
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.8"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">git-multibranch</span> flips along
the same path. <span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.9"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">polyglot-c-py</span>,
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.10"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">polyglot-rust-c</span>,
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.11"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">pytorch-model-recovery</span>, and
<span id="A3.SS1.SSS4.Px2.p1.1.12"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mteb-retrieve</span> flip via the
middleware path: in each, the FRAMEWORK reminder injected before the
next model turn carries enough salience for the agent to fix the
violation rather than publish over it. Iteration 8’s overall score lands
at 76.97, the run’s high-water mark on
Figure <span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self">LABEL:fig:evolution-curve</span>,
and the single biggest jump of the run.

</div>

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS2" class="section ltx_subsection">

### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Changes shipped on the four winning rounds

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1" class="section ltx_subsubsection">

#### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.1 </span>Iteration 2: prompt rules and shell-timeout argument

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">

The Evolve Agent’s response after iteration 1 was two changes. Change
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-1</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">c0b8a05</span> is a 68-line append
to <span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">workspace/systemprompt.md</span>
with no mention of SQLite, WAL, or <span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">db-wal-recovery</span>; the
appended block contains eight numbered rules covering
acceptance-contract extraction, evaluator mirroring, minimal-edit
semantics, candidate scoring, generalization, time budgeting, end-state
readiness, and a stop rule. Change <span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-2</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS1.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">169c34c</span> is a
tool-implementation edit that exposes the shell timeout as a per-call
argument with a higher ceiling, addressing a class of failures in which
the seed harness silently truncated long-running setup commands. Both
manifest entries appear in Figure <a href="#A3.F7" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 7 ‣ C.2.1 Iteration 2: prompt rules and shell-timeout argument ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>.

</div>

<figure id="A3.F7" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<span class="ltx_inline-block"><img

id="A3.F7.pic1"

produced by the evolve agent, then enter Phase 3 of the next round as

predicted fixes do not materialize.</figcaption>
</figure>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2" class="section ltx_subsubsection">

#### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.2 </span>Iteration 5: publish-state mechanism (prompt rules + shell-tool guard)

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">

The Evolve Agent shipped two complementary changes at the iteration-4
boundary, both written for iteration 5. Change
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-7</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">3ba3a90</span> edits
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">workspace/systemprompt.md</span>
together with the descriptor of <span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">run_shell_command</span>; it adds
three rules to the harness’s working memory: a publish-state rule that
names the post-acceptance filesystem state as the deliverable surface, a
scratch-directory rule for tasks with constrained delivery layouts, and
a literal-output rule for DSL, config, and script outputs in which
equivalence is judged at the byte level. Change
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-8</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">4e0aab9</span> edits
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.7"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">workspace/tools/shell_tools/run_shell_command.py</span>;
it installs a stateful publish-state guard inside the shell tool with
three behaviors. First, when the shell observes a successful
evaluator-style final check, it parses the acceptance command for
explicit file paths and roots and records them as protected. Second,
when a later command would delete a protected output or reset a
protected root, the guard intercepts the command before execution and
returns a targeted error explaining which protected target is at risk.
Third, the guard accepts an explicit <span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.8"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ALLOW_POST_SUCCESS_RESET</span>
token from the agent that downgrades the block to a warning and forces
the agent to revalidate before submitting. The two changes are paired by
design: <span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.9"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-7</span> tells the model what
publish state is, <span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p1.1.10"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-8</span> stops the agent from
destroying it even when the model forgets the rule. Both manifest
entries appear in Figure <a href="#A3.F8" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 8 ‣ C.2.2 Iteration 5: publish-state mechanism (prompt rules + shell-tool guard) ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.

</div>

<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<span class="ltx_inline-block"><img

id="A3.F8.pic1"
class="ltx_picture ltx_align_left ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel" /></span>

id="A3.F8.pic2"
class="ltx_picture ltx_align_left ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel" /></span>

<figcaption><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 8: </span>The
two change-manifest entries written together at the iteration-4 boundary
and shipped as the iteration-5 harness. <span id="A3.F8.9.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-7</span> names the
publish-state rule in the system prompt and tool descriptor; <span
id="A3.F8.10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-8</span>
installs the execution-time interlock inside the shell tool. The pair
flips <span id="A3.F8.11.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">path-tracing</span> on the next
round.</figcaption>
</figure>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS3" class="section ltx_subsubsection">

#### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.3 </span>Iteration 6: protected entrypoints and execution-risk middleware

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">

The Evolve Agent shipped two complementary changes for iteration 6.
Change <span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-1</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ff0cf3d</span> extends the
publish-state guard so that script entrypoints tied to the named
evaluator become protected after a passing check, with an explicit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ALLOW_POST_SUCCESS_RESET</span>
token required to override; the token at every successful submit in the
passing rollout is the externally visible evidence that the guard is
engaged, not silently bypassed. Change <span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-2</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">9651986</span> introduces the
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ExecutionRiskHintsMiddleware</span>;
the middleware watches the live sequence of shell commands and tool
outputs and emits a targeted note when it detects any of seven
cross-step risk patterns: shallow validation that relies on
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.7"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">-h</span>,
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.8"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">py_compile</span>, or pure
existence checks; localhost-only service validation when the contract
names an external endpoint; inline or self-written proxy validators
replacing a named evaluator; lower-level model or internal API access
when the contract names a specific wrapper; benchmark checks with no
explicit golden or threshold comparator; repeated long runs that have
already exhausted budget for a known failure mode; and repeated retries
against the same error. The two patterns relevant to trajectory 3 are
inline-proxy validation and shallow validation, which together cover the
F1 to F5 sequence: the grid-integration proxy and the kill of
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.9"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">analysis.R</span> are the
proxy-validator pattern, and the file-existence sweep without a
tolerance comparator is the shallow-validation pattern. The shell tool
change covers F4 specifically: with <span id="A3.SS2.SSS3.p1.1.10"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">analysis.R</span> now protected,
the kill becomes a guarded action that requires the override token and
forces a revalidation pass before submit. Both manifest entries appear
in Figure <a href="#A3.F9" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 9 ‣ C.2.3 Iteration 6: protected entrypoints and execution-risk middleware ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>.

</div>

<figure id="A3.F9" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<span class="ltx_inline-block"><img
src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,"
id="A3.F9.pic1"
class="ltx_picture ltx_align_left ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel" /></span>
</div>
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<span class="ltx_inline-block"><img
src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,"
id="A3.F9.pic2"
class="ltx_picture ltx_align_left ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel" /></span>
</div>
</div>
<figcaption><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 9: </span>The
two change-manifest entries shipped as the iteration-6 harness. <span
id="A3.F9.13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-1</span>
extends the iteration-5 publish-state guard from deliverable files to
script entrypoints, the missing piece that protects <span
id="A3.F9.14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">analysis.R</span>
in <span id="A3.F9.15.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">mcmc-sampling-stan</span>. <span
id="A3.F9.16.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-2</span>
introduces the first cross-step component in this run, namely the <span
id="A3.F9.17.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ExecutionRiskHintsMiddleware</span>
watching the live command history for seven risk patterns.</figcaption>
</figure>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS4" class="section ltx_subsubsection">

#### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.4 </span>Iteration 8: hard blocks and FRAMEWORK reminders

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1" class="ltx_para">

The Evolve Agent shipped two changes for iteration 8 that explicitly
keep the prior architecture and patch its weak points. Change
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-1</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ca35f53</span> edits
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.3"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">workspace/tools/shell_tools/run_shell_command.py</span>
and upgrades two soft reasons to hard blocks: deletion of any
non-<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/tmp</span> protected output is now
a hard block, and reset of any non-<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.5"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">/tmp</span> protected root is now a
hard block. The <span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.6"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ALLOW_POST_SUCCESS_RESET</span>
token can still downgrade other classes of post-success interlocks but
can no longer wipe verified live deliverables or empty live roots.
Change <span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.7"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-2</span> at commit
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.8"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">a4a4a29</span> edits
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.9"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">workspace/middleware/execution_risk_hints.py</span>
and adds three behaviors. First, a new <span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.10"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">before_model</span> hook promotes
any execution-risk note emitted on the previous step into a FRAMEWORK
reminder visible in the next model turn, so the warning becomes part of
the reasoning context rather than text appended after the tool output.
Second, the middleware infers two contract types once per task from the
user request: clean-layout or single-file delivery contracts, and
official-wrapper or named-revision contracts. Third, the middleware adds
two contract-aware after-tool heuristics: a warning when the agent
compiles or builds inside a clean-layout live tree, and a warning when
the contract names an official wrapper or revision but the command uses
a raw <span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.11"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">SentenceTransformer</span> or
<span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.12"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">AutoModel</span> style API instead.
Both changes are deliberately scoped: <span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.13"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-1</span> prevents the
destructive shell command itself, <span id="A3.SS2.SSS4.p1.1.14"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-2</span> makes the right
warning impossible to overlook on the very next model turn. Both
manifest entries appear in Figure <a href="#A3.F10" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 10 ‣ C.2.4 Iteration 8: hard blocks and FRAMEWORK reminders ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.

</div>

<figure id="A3.F10" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">

<span class="ltx_inline-block"><img
src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,"

class="ltx_picture ltx_align_left ltx_centering ltx_figure_panel" /></span>
</div>

<figcaption><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 10: </span>Two
change-manifest entries written together at the iteration-7 boundary and
shipped as the iteration-8 harness. <span id="A3.F10.11.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-1</span> hardens the existing
publish-state shell guard so that the override token can no longer wipe
verified live deliverables. <span id="A3.F10.12.2"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-2</span> makes execution-risk
warnings impossible to overlook at the next model turn and adds two
contract-aware heuristics. Both are deliberately scoped: <span
id="A3.F10.13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-1</span>
prevents the destructive command itself, <span id="A3.F10.14.4"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">chg-2</span> fixes the salience gap
of the iteration-6 middleware.</figcaption>
</figure>

</div>

</div>

<div id="A3.SS3" class="section ltx_subsection">

### <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Reading the change-manifest figures

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">

The trajectories above track individual edits through individual tasks.
The change-manifest carries each edit along with its predicted fixes,
predicted regressions, and constraint level into Phase 3 of the next
iteration, where the attribution check decides whether to keep or roll
it back. One manifest figure is attached to each of the four winning
rounds, all in the same Files / What changed / Failure pattern fixed /
Predicted fixes layout. Figure <a href="#A3.F7" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 7 ‣ C.2.1 Iteration 2: prompt rules and shell-timeout argument ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> shows iteration 2’s prompt
edit and shell-tool edit written together in the seed round.
Figure <a href="#A3.F8" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 8 ‣ C.2.2 Iteration 5: publish-state mechanism (prompt rules + shell-tool guard) ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> shows iteration 5’s
prompt-and-descriptor rule and shell-guard installation that introduce
the publish-state mechanism. Figure <a href="#A3.F9" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 9 ‣ C.2.3 Iteration 6: protected entrypoints and execution-risk middleware ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows iteration 6’s extension
of the publish-state guard to script entrypoints and the introduction of
the cross-step <span id="A3.SS3.p1.1.1"
class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">ExecutionRiskHintsMiddleware</span>.
Figure <a href="#A3.F10" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 10 ‣ C.2.4 Iteration 8: hard blocks and FRAMEWORK reminders ‣ C.2 Changes shipped on the four winning rounds ‣ Appendix C Qualitative Case Study ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> shows iteration 8’s
keep-and-improve patches that close the override-token loophole on the
guard and promote middleware reminders into a FRAMEWORK note visible at
the next model turn. Together the four figures cover three of the four
constraint levels the evolve agent uses, namely prompt, tool
implementation, and middleware, all written in the same JSON shape and
all subject to the same automatic rollback if their predicted fixes do
not appear.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<div id="A4" class="section ltx_appendix">

## <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Per-round Self-attribution Breakdown

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">

This appendix expands the aggregate self-attribution result of
§<a href="#S4.SS4.SSS2" class="ltx_ref"
title="4.4.2 RQ3b: how reliably the loop’s self-attribution tracks reality ‣ 4.4 RQ3: Analysis ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4.2</span></a> with a per-round breakdown
across the four fix/regression by precision/recall panels.

</div>

<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para">

<a href="#A4.F11" class="ltx_ref"
title="In Appendix D Per-round Self-attribution Breakdown ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Figures</span>˜<span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">11</span></a>
and <a href="#A4.F12" class="ltx_ref"
title="Figure 12 ‣ Appendix D Per-round Self-attribution Breakdown ‣ Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses"><span
class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> show the per-round breakdown
across the four fix/regression by precision/recall panels. Bars
decompose each denominator, predicted for precision and actual for
recall, into deep-blue TP versus pale FP or FN; the dashed line traces
the metric on the right-hand $`0`$ to $`100\%`$ axis, and the solid line
shows contemporaneous pass@1. Fix-precision and fix-recall both swing
from near-zero to near-saturation across rounds, so the evolve model’s
causal attribution for its own improvements is informative if noisy.
Regression predictions instead stay near the floor, below $`25\%`$ on
most rounds: across the 9 rounds the agent issued 43 unique regression
predictions and only 5 landed, giving cumulative $`P=11.6\%`$, while 40
regressions the agent did not foresee actually occurred, giving
cumulative $`R=11.1\%`$.

</div>
